purpose: Teach: 健二/シェル/獣医/さようなら/ドック/アルプス/土俵/囲碁

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃の同僚、健二さん、本気で、頼もしい人だったよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?本当に、絶対、本気で、思い出すよ、いつも、本気。
lines.en: You remember Kenji from back when we were young? He was such a dependable man. A real standout.
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Gentle inquiry without pressure. Slow, measured pace as if reaching back through decades. Voice settles on the memory with quiet affection.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。新婚旅行、海で、シェル、二人で、本気で、たくさん、拾ったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本当に、ロマンチック、絶対、本気で、絶対。
lines.en: Yes, I do. On our honeymoon—the shells we collected on the beach, just the two of us. That was so romantic.
lines.style: Immediate warmth, eyes brightening behind the words. Slight lift as she recalls the shared detail. Tender cadence, as if reliving the moment even as she speaks it. No rush.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔、飼ってた犬、獣医さんに、本気で、お世話になったわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?家族、皆、感謝、絶対、本気で、本当に。
lines.en: And that old dog we had—the vet was so good to us. Do you remember? The whole family was grateful.
lines.style: Pause after the opening image, as if seeing the dog clearly. Voice softens with care. Deliberate on 'grateful'—weight of remembered kindness. Slight tremor of gentle feeling.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃の友達、さようならの時、本気で、寂しかったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本当に、絶対、また、会いたいわね、絶対、本気で、本当に。
lines.en: Friends from those days… saying goodbye to them was so hard. Do you remember? I still wish we could see them again.
lines.style: Quieter register, a note of real sadness underneath. The longing is genuine, not performed. Trails off slightly on the wish, as if it's still alive in her.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、若い頃、船のドック、本気で、働いていたんだって、ばあさん、覚えてる?本当に、苦労、絶対、本気で、感謝、絶対。
lines.en: Your grandfather worked at the shipyard when he was young, didn't he? Do you remember? We were always grateful for how hard he worked.
lines.style: Respectful, almost reverent tone. Deliberate on the labor and sacrifice. Voice carries admiration mixed with a quiet melancholy. Slight emphasis on 'grateful' as if paying homage.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、新婚旅行、本気で、アルプス、行きたかったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?結局、別の場所だったけれども、絶対、本気で、思い出。
lines.en: We wanted to go to the Alps for our honeymoon, remember? We ended up somewhere else in the end, but those memories stayed with us.
lines.style: Wistful but not regretful. A gentle smile audible in the tone. The voice softens around 'memories'—tender acceptance of what was, not resentment at what wasn't. Quiet resolve.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、相撲の土俵、本気で、若い頃、見に行ったことあるって、ばあさん、覚えてる?本気で、絶対、面白い、お話、本気。
lines.en: Your grandfather actually went to see a sumo tournament when he was young. Do you remember? He used to tell the best stories about it.
lines.style: Slight brightness returns—genuine pleasure in the remembered anecdote. Voice lifts with pride in him. Conversational but reflective, as if he's right there in the story.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、二人で、囲碁、本気で、対戦したわよね、覚えてる、あなた?私、本気で、負けたわよね、悔しかった、本気で、絶対、本当に。
lines.en: When we were young, the two of us played go together. Do you remember? I lost every time—it was so frustrating.
lines.style: Soft laugh underneath, slightly self-deprecating. Tender embarrassment about the losses. The word 'frustrated' carries real feeling but softened by time and affection. Intimate, as if sharing a small secret.
